benchmarks.title: Automated Novelty Assessment in Scientific Literature via Semantic Embeddings and Citation Contexts
benchmarks.venue: Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP)
benchmarks.abstract: Determining whether a newly submitted scientific paper presents genuinely novel ideas is a critical yet time-consuming task for peer reviewers. We propose an automated novelty evaluation framework combining dense passage representations and local citation subgraph topology. Using a contrastive learning objective, our model identifies subtle conceptual shifts between proposed methodologies and prior art. Experimental evaluation across 14,000 computer science papers demonstrates a 78% correlation with expert peer-review novelty scores.

benchmarks.title: SciFact: Fact-Checking and Comparative Evidence Retrieval over Research Papers
benchmarks.abstract: We address the challenge of scientific claim verification and comparative evidence retrieval. Given a scientific claim, the task is to retrieve relevant evidence abstracts from research literature and predict whether the evidence supports, refutes, or is neutral towards the claim. We introduce SciFact, a dataset of 1.4K expert-annotated claims paired with PubMed abstracts, and develop baseline neural models for grounded scientific reasoning.

benchmarks.title: SciBERT: A Pretrained Language Model for Scientific Text
benchmarks.abstract: Obtaining pre-trained models on specialized domain corpora has proven advantageous across numerous natural language processing tasks. In this work, we present SciBERT, a pre-trained language model based on BERT, trained on a large multi-domain corpus of scientific publications from Semantic Scholar. SciBERT demonstrates substantial performance improvements on scientific classification, citation prediction, and sequence labeling tasks.

benchmarks.title: Can Large Language Models Identify Novel Scientific Hypotheses? A Systematic Benchmark
benchmarks.abstract: Recent breakthroughs in generative language modeling have spurred interest in LLM-assisted scientific discovery. In this study, we systematically evaluate whether frontier LLMs can discern true scientific novelty from repackaged incremental variations. We construct a curated benchmark of paired accepted papers and rejected resubmissions. We find that while raw zero-shot prompting yields high false-positive novelty rates, retrieval-augmented grounding reduces hallucinated novelty assessments by 42%.

benchmarks.title: Citation Graph Neural Networks for Detecting Paradigm Shifts and Emerging Topics
benchmarks.abstract: Detecting emerging research trends and disruptive contributions requires tracking the co-evolution of semantic content and network citation topologies. We present CiteGNN, an inductive graph neural network that encodes both dynamic citation flow and semantic abstract similarities. Our model outperforms static centrality baselines by 19% in predicting long-term citation momentum and identifying foundational paradigm shifts early in publication life-cycles.

benchmarks.title: Emergence of Scaling in Random Networks
benchmarks.abstract: Systems as diverse as genetic networks or the World Wide Web are organized into complex networks whose vertices represent system elements and edges represent interactions. Here we demonstrate that common properties of diverse complex networks arise from continuous expansion and preferential attachment, producing power-law degree distributions.

benchmarks.title: Collective Dynamics of 'Small-World' Networks
benchmarks.abstract: Networks of coupled dynamical systems model complex systems in biology, physics, and sociology. Here we explore small-world networks that are highly clustered, like regular lattices, yet have small characteristic path lengths, like random graphs. We show that dynamic systems on small-world networks exhibit enhanced signal-propagation speed and computational power.

sample_proposals.title: Automatic Research Novelty Assessment Using Large Language Models, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and Citation Graph Analysis
sample_proposals.keywords: Research Novelty Assessment, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Citation Graph Analysis, Semantic Embeddings, Scientific Peer Review
sample_proposals.abstract: Evaluating the novelty of proposed research proposals and manuscript submissions is a high-stakes, labor-intensive responsibility in peer review and funding allocation. Current manual evaluation methods struggle to keep pace with the exponential growth of scientific literature, resulting in redundant research and overlooked prior art. In this paper, we propose a hybrid automated novelty assessment architecture combining three complementary analytical paradigms: dense semantic embeddings for conceptual literature matching, a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline for grounded comparative passage reasoning, and a citation graph topology analyzer to quantify network centrality and cross-disciplinary bridge novelty. Our system computes an explainable multi-dimensional novelty score (0-100) underpinned by verified vs. potential gap classification across objectives, methodologies, datasets, and target domains.
sample_proposals.objectives:
1. Ingest research proposals via text input or parsed PDF documents.
2. Retrieve relevant peer-reviewed literature dynamically via OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar APIs without hallucination.
3. Compute semantic vector similarity between proposed contributions and existing abstracts.
4. Apply RAG to extract grounded evidence passages and perform comparative literature analysis.
5. Classify research gaps across 5 dimensions (objectives, methods, datasets, domain, contributions).
6. Construct NetworkX citation subgraphs to evaluate graph centrality and citation bridges.
7. Generate an explainable, documented novelty score with interactive dashboards and exportable reports.

sample_proposals.title: Targeted Cancer Drug Repurposing via Graph Transformer Networks and Molecular Multi-Task Learning
sample_proposals.keywords: Drug Repurposing, Graph Transformers, Molecular Multi-Task Learning, Oncology, Virtual Screening
sample_proposals.abstract: De novo drug discovery typically requires 10 to 15 years and billions of dollars. Drug repurposing offers an accelerated alternative by identifying new therapeutic indications for approved compounds. We develop an end-to-end Graph Transformer architecture that jointly models chemical 3D conformers and disease-gene heterogeneous interactome networks. By utilizing multi-task learning across 120 kinase targets, our model predicts binding affinities and cell-line viability in refractory pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, validated via in vitro cytotoxicity assays.
sample_proposals.objectives:
1. Construct a heterogeneous biomedical knowledge graph combining drug molecules, target proteins, and clinical indications.
2. Train an SE(3)-equivariant Graph Transformer on 3D conformational molecular features.
3. Evaluate repurposing candidates against resistant pancreatic cancer cell lines.

sample_proposals.title: Ultra-Low Power Multimodal Vision-Language Inference on Resource-Constrained Edge Microcontrollers
sample_proposals.keywords: Edge AI, TinyML, Quantization, Multimodal Transformers, Microcontrollers, Visual Grounding
sample_proposals.abstract: Deploying multimodal vision-language models on microcontrollers with less than 2 megabytes of SRAM has historically been considered infeasible due to extreme memory and compute bottlenecks. We propose MicroVLM, a sub-10M parameter vision-language model trained using progressive integer-only 2-bit weight and 4-bit activation quantization with neural architecture search tailored for ARM Cortex-M55 microcontrollers. MicroVLM achieves real-time visual grounding at 18 frames per second drawing less than 65 milliwatts.
sample_proposals.objectives:
1. Design a sub-10M parameter hybrid convolutional-attention multimodal backbone.
2. Formulate 2-bit weight quantization aware training with hardware-aware scheduling.
3. Deploy and benchmark real-time inference on an ARM Cortex-M55 edge microcontroller platform.
